text.text: Cassis and cedar, still tightly wound — gave it three hours and it opened into something generous.

headline.text: A Bordeaux blend that argues with its own reputation.

standfirst.text: Dryland vines on decomposed granite, whole-berry into open concrete, eighteen months in old French oak.

essay.text: The fruit comes off a single block on the Stellenbosch side of the estate, planted long before anyone was picking for acid, and never trellised — so the vines carry their own canopy and ripen slowly in their own shade.
The structure is where the estate’s hand shows. Tannin is fine-grained rather than grippy, and the alcohol never announces itself.

quote.text: We stopped picking for colour in 2011. The moment we started picking for acid, the vineyard told us what it actually was.

text.text: The fynbos note is not a marketing fiction — it is in the glass, and it is the reason this wine cannot be made anywhere else.
Poured it blind beside a village Côte-Rôtie for a table of six. Four preferred the De Toren.
